Definition: Ashshur, the second son of Shem; also his descendants and the country occupied by them (i.e. Assyria), its region and its empire
BiblicalUsage: Asshur is the son of Shem, and the nation and the land that bear his name, and it grows from a man into an empire. Out of the land of Shinar went forth Asshur and builded Nineveh, Isaiah calls Assyria the rod of God's anger and the staff of His indignation, and in the days of Hezekiah Sennacherib king of Assyria comes up against the fenced cities of Judah.
TheologicalSignificance: A name that grows from a son of Shem to the rod of God's anger tells me how God uses nations: Assyria is His staff to punish, and then His staff is broken for its pride. And I hold that the God who raised Assyria up is the God who shuts its king outside the walls of Jerusalem.
